text: There are three types of false experience, distinguished by doubt, error, and inference. Knowledge that apprehends the coexistence of contradictory attributes in a single object is doubt, as in the case of “Is that a post or a man?” False knowledge is error, as in the case of “This is silver” when it is actually shell. Inference is the attribution of the pervader based on the attribution of the pervaded, as in the case of “If there were no fire, there would be no smoke either.”
